events.note: 1 Jan 1740 (bridging): the annexation of May 1739. 'Nader Shah annexes all lands west of the Indus river and establishes hegemony over the region' (infobox) and, leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739, 'he ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'. The 1739 Mughal loss was paired with afsharid-iran/ledger/12 (Sindh only), so the p1740 anchor still holds these cells as Mughal and mughal-empire_1740 then drops them to nobody for one year before afsharid-iran_1741 adds them back.

region.text: Courland and Semigallia, the duchy's land of the 1734-1771 shape

events.note: Restores the duchy's land, which is nobody's in the p1740 anchor (the duchy holds 4 of its 122 cells; russian-empire ledger/1 took 113 of them in 1721 and Russia's later shapes do not hold them). The page describes no loss of Courland territory between 1700 and 1795: the duchy was 'incorporated into the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1726' and 'annexed by the Russian Empire' on 24 October 1795; Biron's exile (1741) and the dukes Louis Ernest of Brunswick (June 1741) and Charles of Saxony changed the duke, not the land. The vassal tint comes from hierarchy.csv (duchy-of-courland of the Commonwealth, 1569-1795).

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 1741 shape restores Lahore, Multan and the Pakistani Punjab east of the Indus but not Delhi: the Cliopatria Mughal shape of 1741 (1.67 M km2) has a hole where its Afsharid shape of 1741 (3.43 M km2, 473 Indian cells) covers Delhi, Haryana and the Indian Punjab, and the compiled map shows Mughal land as nobody's for 1741-1743 and Mughal again from 1744 (339 cells added). Page: before leaving Delhi on 16 May 1739 Nader 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'; the Afsharid dossier already removes these cells from its own 1741 shape.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1744 shape without Azov (ceded to Russia in 1739), plus the Iraqi Kurdistan, Mosul and Hakkari cells that its 1744-1747 shape gives to nobody while its 1741 and 1748 shapes hold them

keyframe_overrides.why: The compiled map drops 98 Ottoman cells (As-Sulaymaniyah 64, Ninawa 19, Hakkari 7) to nobody in 1744-1747, where Cliopatria's Afsharid shape of 1744 covers them, and gives them back in 1748. The war page: Nader 'captured Kirkuk, Erbil and besieged Mosul on 14 September 1743'; the siege lasted 40 days and the pasha 'successfully defended Mosul and Nader Shah was forced to retreat'; at Kerden (September 1746) 'The boundaries were unchanged and Baghdad remained in Ottoman hands' (status quo ante bellum). Kirkuk and Erbil stay a contest (ledger 1743-1746); the page does not mention Sulaymaniyah or Hakkari being taken.

correction.text: the 1744 shape with the Kashmir Valley restored (as in the dossier), plus the Punjab east of the Indus and the Delhi hinterland that Cliopatria's 1744 Mughal shape leaves empty: the Mughals held them until Ahmad Shah's campaigns of 1748

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 1741 keyframe holds the Punjab east of the Indus (Nader 'ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus' in 1739) and its 1748 keyframe is Mughal again, but the 1744 keyframe (Cliopatria's shape without them) drops 124 Pakistani Punjab cells, 7 Azad Kashmir cells and about 100 Haryana and Indian Punjab cells to nobody for 1744-1747. Ahmad Shah Durrani page: the Mughals under Shah Nawaz were defeated at Lahore on 11 January 1748 and Moin-ul-Mulk, 'the new governor of Punjab', ceded revenues in November 1748; the Punjab as far as Sirhind passed to the Durrani only by the treaty signed on 3 April 1752, 'ending Mughal rule in Punjab'. So the Mughal Punjab is nobody's by a gap in the shape, not by an event.
